The chitra veena, also called gottuvadhyam, is a fretless lute-type veena of South Indian Carnatic music, a chordophone. The body follows the modern South Indian veena, usually with six melody strings, three drone strings and eleven or twelve sympathetic strings. It is played with a pick held between the index and middle fingers of the right hand on the metal melody strings, while the left hand slides a cylindrical block of hardwood, buffalo horn, glass, steel or Teflon along the strings to change pitch. It was named and brought back to the concert platform by Sakha Rama Rao, and is now mostly used for Carnatic solos, world-music collaborations and musical dialogues between north and south India.
齊特拉維那琴為卡納提克音樂中的無品弦鳴樂器，音色主要由六條旋律弦、三條持續音弦與: The chitra veena is a fretless chordophone of Carnatic music; its sound comes from six melody strings, three drone strings and eleven or twelve sympathetic strings. The player plucks the metal melody strings with a pick and slides a block along them with the left hand to change pitch, so the melodic line is continuous and close to the voice. The main strings are set as three tonics, two fifths and one basic tonic, and include octave strings, producing a distinctive resonance. Compared with the Saraswati veena, the drone strings are tuned similarly; compared with the sitar, the sympathetic strings are tuned similarly, but the arrangement of the top melody strings differs. 齊特拉維那琴的早期記載可追溯至《納提亞沙斯特拉》所列七弦無品樂器，後見於《桑吉塔: Early records of the chitra veena go back to the seven-string fretless instruments listed in the 《Natya Shastra》, and it later appears in the 《Sangita Ratnakara》. As the fretless lute-type veena of modern South Indian Carnatic music, it was named and brought back to the concert platform by Sakha Rama Rao around the end of the nineteenth and the beginning of the twentieth century. His pupil Gottuvadhyam Narayana Iyengar raised its standing as a performance instrument, and his son Narasimhan spread its tuning and playing method. The instrument later developed into the South Indian veena form and produced variants such as the navachitra veena.
